title: VISTA’s view of the Small Magellanic Cloud
caption: The Small Magellanic Cloud, imaged by ESO's VISTA telescope
celestial: Small Magellanic Cloud, SMC · constellation Tucana · about 200000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Millions of stars fill every part of this frame, a very wide infrared view of the Small Magellanic Cloud, a neighboring galaxy about 200,000 light-years away in Tucana. It was taken with ESO's VISTA survey telescope and is the biggest infrared image ever made of the SMC.

The SMC stands out in the southern sky and is visible without any telescope. However, clouds of interstellar dust keep visible-light telescopes from getting a really clear look at what lies inside it. VISTA's infrared capabilities let astronomers see the galaxy's countless stars far more clearly than ever before.

Besides the SMC itself, VISTA picked up plenty of background galaxies and a number of star clusters, among them the very bright globular cluster 47 Tucanae on the right. A globular cluster is a dense ball of old stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (354.37 x 313.48 arcminutes) and distance (200000 light years), the frame spans roughly 21,000 × 18,000 light-years. Its light set out about 200,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: VISTA's VIRCAM camera observed in near-infrared light through Y, J and Ks filters. The color mapping isn't published.
